newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania jails journalists for Iliescu KGB story.
newsitem.headline: Romania jails journalists for Iliescu KGB story.

text.p: Two Romanian journalists were ordered jailed on Friday on charges of defaming President Ion Iliescu by alleging he once spied for the Soviet KGB secret service.

A Bucharest court official said the director general of the daily newspaper Ziua, Sorin Rosca Stanescu, was sentenced to a year in prison and one of his journalists, Tana Ardeleanu, to 14 months for "defaming state authority".
The court ruling also stripped the two journalists of their civil rights, including the right to practise their profession.
The pair said they stood by a series of stories run last year on Iliescu, who leads in opinion surveys to win re-election in November polls. Both said they would appeal the verdict.

"We have not attacked a representative of state authority, since our disclosures referred to Ion Iliescu while he was a student and not as president of Romania," Stanescu said after the verdict was announced.
He said legal procedures had been violated because the defence had not been allowed to produce any witnesses "while the prosecution had no fewer than eight".
The sentences far exceeded prosecution recommendations of a six-month suspended term for both journalists, and lawyers said such a decision was highly unusual in post-Communist Romania.

Iliescu has emphatically denied allegations that he was recruited by the now-defunct KGB while a student in Moscow in the early 1950s. Russian officials denied that the man presented in the articles as the spymaster "controlling" Iliescu had ever worked for the KGB.
Iliescu's staff were unavaliable to comment.

Defence lawyers failed to produce concrete evidence to back their claim during the proceedings and said incriminating documents and tapes had been stolen. Witnesses in court said some evidence produced by the defendants had been fabricated.

The journalists had been charged with "producing grave insults to the institution of the presidency through forged documents" under a controversial law against defamation of an institution rather than an individual.
Their reports also held Iliescu "morally responsible" for many of more than 1,000 deaths during the December 1989 uprising which ousted Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
Iliescu was a communist official who served in a variety of capacities under Ceausescu, including the head of a publishing house during the December 1989 events.
He emerged from the upheaval at the head of the National Salvation Front and won elections in 1990 and 1992.
